subject: Residency & tiered-retention: proposed split-storage + archive-trigger Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Brown <alice.brown@finbank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Leigh <thomas.leigh@finbank.com>
Date: Sat, 09 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed DPA redline: split residency + archives outside EU

Connor,

Thanks for the quick intro call last week. Attached is FinBank's proposed redline to the DPA focused on two items we flagged during procurement: (1) primary data residency inside the EU, and (2) limited ability to store backups/archives outside the EU under tightly controlled conditions. High level asks:

- Primary customer data (customer-submitted content and profile data) must be processed and stored in the EU (EEA).
- Backups and immutable snapshots may be held outside the EU for up to 90 days for operational restore, but only if: encrypted with customer-controlled KMS; access credentials restricted to named Redwood staff; and documented erasure can be provided on request.
- Audit/logging: we need 30 days of request/response logs retained in the US for operational troubleshooting. We are open to pseudonymization of logs if feasible.
- Evidence: procurement will require a representative erasure certificate for snapshots, and a short paper on your archive trigger / retention automation flow.

Attached: FinBank-DPA-proposed-redline-20280908.pdf

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (A) guarantee primary EU storage, (B) agree to the proposed constraints for out-of-region backups, and (C) provide a feasible approach for log pseudonymization? Please include the engineering and legal leads so we have a consolidated answer for our procurement committee (they're on CC).

Thanks,
Alice Brown
Director, Cloud Procurement
FinBank

---

(Attachment: FinBank-DPA-proposed-redline-20280908.pdf, 12 pages PDF containing redline suggestions and proposed language.)

Alice — thanks for the clear redline. Looping in legal and infra to confirm details (cc'd internally). High-level: we can commit to primary EU storage for customer data. Backups/archives outside EU are possible but we need to align on KMS controls and the operational process to generate deletion certificates.

Quick clarifying Q for you: are the 90 days a hard requirement or a maximum window you are willing to accept if we provide more strict controls (e.g., segregated dedicated buckets and documented access logging)? Also, on logs — is pseudonymization acceptable in lieu of raw logs for the 30-day troubleshooting window, or do you require full raw logs for certain investigations?

I attached a short set of notes from our call with initial positions. We'll follow up with a consolidated response by Monday EOD (your time) after legal and infra weigh in.

Best,

Subject: RE: Residency & tiered-retention: proposed split-storage + archive-trigger Q&A

Team — quick legal read on FinBank's redline and our negotiation posture:

Summary of recommended stance:
- Primary data in EU: acceptable, we can contractually bind processing + primary storage location to EEA regions.
- Backups/archives outside EU: cannot accept an unrestricted out-of-region retention clause. We should offer a constrained compromise: allow out-of-region backup/archives only under the following cumulative controls:
  * Customer-managed KMS (customer holds the root keys; Redwood uses envelope encryption with customer KMS).
  * Physical/tenant segregation: archives must be written to dedicated, customer-scoped buckets/accounts (no mixed-tenant archives).
  * Access restrictions: list of named Redwood roles allowed access; any access to archives requires documented justification and is logged.
  * Retention ceiling and erasure certification: maximum 90 days outside EU, with an automated archive-trigger workflow that produces a deletion certificate on erasure request within 7 business days.
- Logging/pseudonymization: acceptable alternative to raw logs if FinBank will provide a salt or tokenization mapping under control of the customer. Otherwise, for critical incident investigations, we may need ability to produce more detailed traces under Data Subject/Legal process.

Suggested clause language (to put in our counter):
"Backup and archive copies: Notwithstanding Section X (Data Residency), Provider may store encrypted backup and archive copies outside the European Economic Area for a temporary period not to exceed 90 days solely for operational restore purposes. Such copies shall: (i) be encrypted using Customer-controlled KMS; (ii) be stored in customer-dedicated storage; (iii) be accessible only to persons named in Appendix Y and only upon documented operational need; and (iv) be capable of being comprehensively deleted upon Customer request with Provider producing a deletion certificate within seven (7) business days."

Action items for infra: @Karthik — can you confirm the technical feasibility of:
1) Writing customer snapshots to a dedicated bucket in a non-EEA region while maintaining envelope encryption with a customer KMS?
2) Producing a machine-verifiable deletion certificate showing deletion of snapshots and verifying zero-length objects (or confirm if object tombstoning delays apply)?

Also, @Lauren — from a security/audit standpoint, we should propose periodic attestation checks and allow for a scoped third-party audit (e.g., for archived snapshots) if FinBank requires.

If infra confirms feasibility, we'll prepare the counter redline and include an operational runbook and sample deletion certificate template for procurement.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redline: split residency + archives outside EU — Redwood response and next steps

Alice / Thomas — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Below is a consolidated response and proposed next steps after internal alignment.

Answer to the three asks:
A) Primary EU storage: YES — Redwood will process and store primary customer data in the EEA for FinBank production tenants. We will add clause language making the region binding for primary data.

B) Backups/archives outside EU: CONDITIONAL YES — Redwood can support backups and immutable snapshots outside the EEA subject to the following controls (these will be reflected in our counter-redline):
  - Customer-managed KMS: Customer retains root KMS control; Redwood uses envelope encryption with the customer key for any out-of-region snapshots.
  - Dedicated buckets/accounts: Snapshots and archives will be written to customer-dedicated storage namespaces that are logically isolated from other customers.
  - Access & logging: Only named Redwood roles may access archives; access requires documented justification and is logged. We will provide sample access logs for procurement.
  - Deletion certificate: On customer request we will run an automated erasure workflow and provide a deletion certificate within 7 business days. Note: due to eventual consistency/tombstoning on some object stores, we will include verifiable evidence (object metadata, deletion marker hashes, and audit log entries).

C) Logs and pseudonymization: We can support pseudonymization/tokenization of operational logs for a standard 30-day troubleshooting window. For high-severity investigations requiring raw traces, we will require a legal process (e.g., court order or an agreed incident request workflow) and will provide those traces under strict controls. If you prefer, we can accept customer-supplied salt/token mapping to support pseudonymization.

Evidence and auditability:
- We will provide our SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted sample deletion certificate.
- We will prepare a short operational runbook that explains the archive-trigger flow (how a snapshot is promoted to archive, retention timers, and erasure process).

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood legal to send a counter-redline with the clause language Naomi suggested (we will attach the sample deletion certificate template).
2) Engineering scoping call (1 week) to confirm technical runbook and timeline.
3) Procurement to confirm whether the 90-day outside-EEA window is acceptable with the safeguards above; if not, we will iterate on maximum window and audit conditions.

Attached is our initial counter redline (Redwood-DPA-counter-20280911.pdf). Please let us know a convenient time this week for a 30-minute call to close the open items.

Best regards,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
